question: Can a fixed zero-DC difference-of-Gaussians source suppress single-realization low-frequency tone drift while retaining positive grain-scale correlation and the unchanged P4AF density marginal?

research_basis.motivation: Low-frequency stochastic error is perceptually objectionable; blue-noise research motivates suppressing low spatial frequencies, but this candidate is a deterministic Gaussian band-pass field rather than a claimed blue-noise mask or measured film NPS.

model.source_field: one coordinate-counter normal field filtered by an equal-weight narrow-minus-broad 2D Gaussian kernel

negative_controls: single narrow Gaussian without zero-DC subtraction

branch_rule.pass: Retain as a generic synthetic band-pass structure candidate and open one independently seeded photographic severe/NPS/value audit.
branch_rule.fail: Close without sigma, weight, seed, marginal, strength or threshold rescue; leave P4AF as the full-resolution synthetic reference and continue another colour or physical mechanism.

forbidden: using sample/image statistics to recenter the field
changing the frozen P4AF marginal or amplitude
calling the field measured film NPS or calibrated grain
photographic rendering before every synthetic gate passes
claim_ceiling: Generic synthetic zero-DC Gaussian-band-pass density structure; not measured film NPS, physical particle geometry, stock response, photographic quality or product evidence.
